neighbours.label: taking a side in a dispute between parties: side with, take sides between, declare for, hand over to or pass on to the other party
fire: The governor openly sided with the mill owners against the striking weavers.
Most of the villages refused to choose sides between the two warring clans.
The neutral kingdom was pressed to declare for one of the rival emperors.
The informant turned the fugitives over to the occupying troops for a reward.
Moscow came out in support of the junta's crackdown on the protesters.
The bishop forwarded the complaint on to the royal court instead of judging it himself.
His cousins urged him to break with the party and join the opposition.
The elders backed the younger brother's claim against the elder's.
quiet: The governor met the mill owners and the weavers to hear their complaints.
Most of the villages lie between the two rivers on the northern plain.
The neutral kingdom traded wool and timber with both empires.
The fugitives hid in the mill for three days before moving on.
Moscow announced a new rail line to the northern ports.
The bishop read the complaint aloud and filed it in the archive.
His cousins urged him to rest before the long journey.
The elders listened to both brothers tell the story of the harvest.

predictions: 3-4/8 fire (probe: take sides between 0.513, handed over to 0.250, pass on to 0.218, urged him to break off 0.139, 'prevent a conflict between' 0.011); near misses under 0.05
notes: The + pole is friendly communication (talk to, chat, converse, relationship). Only 'take sides between' cleared 0.30 in the probe; hand-over and pass-on frames were 0.22-0.25, so this is a weak pole and the label is a best guess at the allegiance theme in the card (support of Beijing's actions, took China's side, handed you over, choose sides).
